payload.title: feat/one-subject-per-run at 0cda2f8: a run subject keeps its patch apart from its inputs (owner reading of R-0HABWN#7)
payload.body: Commit 0cda2f8 on branch feat/one-subject-per-run, from 3ec4979. Applies the owner's return of R-0HABWN#7: an input file is data given to the code, not a patch. A run subject keeps {base, patch, files}; a based Hypothesis subject is held by a run at its base whose patch, if any, is one of its files, so a run at B given inputs covers bare B and a run at B plus a patch never does. Code and tests were written, and go test run, while building, before E's rule; the rule's checks run after it.

why: The candidate that applies the owner's reading of R-0HABWN#7.
0cda2f8 holds 3ec4979 and applies the owner's return of R-0HABWN#7.

payload.body: Supports only if all hold. Rules: R7 a run keeps its patch apart from its inputs (R-0HABWN#7 as returned); R3a-R3d, F1, F3-F6 as E-2XGWNC. R7 also: 3ec4979's exact-files compare restored fails TestRunWithInputsCoversBareBase. (b) go vet, go test -count=1 pass. (c) status, check same bytes: 0cda2f8 vs installed (10540106) on 4 trees; vs 33896ec (2297b148) on 3; sha256s logged, 0cda2f8's differs.

payload.observation: The fresh review of 0cda2f8 against ADR 0020, line 3 and the owner's reading of R-0HABWN#7 gives six findings and one question, each recorded below as a limit; E-6PD9S8's rule outcome does not change. The reviewer also found go vet and go test pass on 0cda2f8.
limits: F1: a Hypothesis tied to B plus arm.patch is covered by a run at bare B with no Arm whose --inputs file has the patch's bytes, though the patch never changed the code.
F2: a Hypothesis tied to B plus an input file I is held by a run at B whose patch is I, because a Hypothesis's subject does not say which of its files is the patch.
F3: replay-spec rule 27 still names 'a subject with no base and no files' and not the new 'no base, no patch and no files' or 'patch ... is not a sha256' rejections.
F4: ADR 0020 still writes a run subject as {base, files} with no patch field, while the code, replay-spec and glossary write {base, patch, files}.
F5: a Result written by a 7257753 or 3ec4979 binary keeps an Arm's patch inside files, so 0cda2f8 replays it as a run at B given input P, which covers bare B.
F6: no test runs rule 26 after the owner's case: once a run at B given inputs holds a bare-B Hypothesis, a new tie of that Hypothesis must be refused with 'subject ran in'.
Q: a sandbox with Arms keeps only patched subjects, so a bare-B control its Launch builds gives no bare-B subject, and a bare-B Hypothesis stays uncovered by it.

why: Records the fresh review's findings on 0cda2f8 as limits of the latest Result.

refers.text: ADR 0020 is the owner's decision record. This run may change only the spec, glossary and principles text it names, so amending the ADR's {base, files} notation to {base, patch, files} is the owner's edit.

Void for every candidate: no log in this repository holds a Result with a subjects field from 7257753 or 3ec4979 (grep of every investigations/*/.tree/events); those commits are unmerged heads of PR #132, so no store has their format.

Outside line 3: a sandbox record names its base and Arms and no control run, so no cited record holds a bare-B control; whether a control build counts as a cited run is a new line, a new Goal for the owner.

why: Three review findings no test within this Goal's lines can close.
